videos.title: The Country That Skipped Friday
videos.facebook_caption:
In Samoa, Friday, December 30, 2011 never happened. 📅

The country went straight from Thursday to Saturday, bringing its calendar into closer alignment with trading partners Australia and New Zealand.

One decision changed the date for an entire country.

#CurioBureau #Samoa #History #Geography

videos.facebook_caption:

videos.title: The Waterfall They Switched Off
videos.facebook_caption:
In 1969, engineers stopped the flow over Niagara’s American Falls. 🌊

They diverted the water so they could examine the rock beneath the waterfall and study the debris piled at its base. Horseshoe Falls kept flowing.

For a few months, a famous curtain of water became an exposed landscape.

videos.title: The Lake That Drained Underground
videos.facebook_caption:

The miners escaped. The lake was never the same.

videos.title: Boston’s Molasses Flood
videos.facebook_caption:
The flood that struck Boston in 1919 was made of molasses.

A storage tank burst in the North End, releasing roughly 2.3 million gallons through the streets. Twenty-one people died.

Behind the strange headline is a serious story about structural failure, ignored warnings and accountability.

#CurioBureau #Boston #History #Engineering

videos.title: The Spacecraft Lost Between Two Units
videos.facebook_caption:
The spacecraft reached Mars. Its signal never came back.

In 1999, a mismatch between pound-force seconds and newton seconds in ground software helped send Mars Climate Orbiter onto the wrong approach.

The failure was bigger than a conversion: the checks that should have caught it failed, too.

#CurioBureau #Space #Engineering #Mars

videos.title: Why Sunlight Is White
videos.facebook_caption:
Sunlight looks white. So why do we picture a yellow Sun? ☀️

Visible sunlight blends many colors. The atmosphere changes the light that reaches us, and some scientific solar images assign colors to wavelengths our eyes cannot see.

A yellow drawing, a red sunset and a colorful solar image are telling different stories.

#CurioBureau #Science #Space #Sun

videos.title: The Height You Can’t Keep
videos.facebook_caption:
Space can make you taller. You don’t get to keep the extra height. 🚀

Astronauts can gain up to about 3% in height as the spine changes under reduced loading in microgravity. Back on Earth, their usual height returns.

The change comes mainly from the spine, rather than new bone growth.

videos.title: Why Your Recorded Voice Sounds Different
videos.facebook_caption:
Why does your recorded voice sound like someone else? 🎙️

When you speak, you hear sound through the air and vibrations through your skull and other tissues. An ordinary microphone captures the airborne route, leaving out part of the experience you know.

The microphone and room affect playback, too. Both versions are you—heard differently.

videos.title: Your Fingers Don’t Just Soak Up Water
videos.facebook_caption:
Your fingers don’t wrinkle in water simply because the skin soaks it up.

The familiar folds involve an active nervous-system response and changes in the blood vessels beneath the skin.

Could the wrinkles help with wet grip? Some studies suggest benefits, but the evidence is mixed. The explanation is more interesting than the usual answer.

videos.title: Why Metal Feels Colder Than Wood
videos.facebook_caption:
Metal can feel colder than wood—even when both are at the same room temperature.

The difference is how quickly heat leaves your warmer hand. Metal carries that heat away more readily, creating a stronger cold sensation.

Your hand feels heat transfer. It isn’t reading a thermometer.

#CurioBureau #Science #Physics

videos.title: Why Mint Feels Cold
videos.facebook_caption:
Mint can send a cold signal without an ice cube. 🌿

Menthol activates TRPM8, a receptor that also responds to cooling. Your nervous system can interpret that activity as a cool sensation.

Feeling cold and measuring a lower temperature aren’t the same thing.

#CurioBureau #Science #HumanBody

A kitchen routine hides a tiny chain reaction.

videos.title: The Notification That Never Happened
videos.facebook_caption:
You felt your phone vibrate. You checked. Nothing.

That familiar false alarm is often called phantom vibration. Research has documented people perceiving phone vibrations that did not happen, though its explanation is still debated.

A sensation can feel convincing even when there is no notification behind it.

#CurioBureau #Science #Perception

videos.title: If the Sun Disappeared, When Would You Notice?
videos.facebook_caption:
If the Sun disappeared, daylight wouldn’t end instantly. ☀️

Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth. In this impossible thought experiment, even the change in Earth’s orbit would take time to arrive.

For those final minutes, we would still be living in the Sun’s past.

The Sun cannot actually vanish; this is a lesson about how information travels.

#CurioBureau #Space #Science #Physics

videos.title: The Dead Star That Could Still Explode
videos.facebook_caption:
A dead star. A falling limit. One more possible ending.

A theoretical black-dwarf model explores how an extremely slow change in composition could make some massive stellar remnants collapse in the far future—if protons do not decay first.

This is a hypothesis, not an observed explosion or a prediction for our Sun.
